latest.title: Made Tech appointed to Met Office Framework
latest.content:
9 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 9160T
Made Tech Group PLC

MADE TECH GROUP PLC
("Made Tech" or the "Group")
Made Tech appointed to new Met Office Delivery Partnerships Framework
Made Tech selected across all three lots targeted, including strategically important Secure Services lot
London, 9 September 2026
-
Made Tech Group Plc
, (AIM:MTEC) a leading provider of digital, data and technology services to the UK public sector, is pleased to announce that it has been selected as one of a list of suppliers to three lots under the Met Office's new Delivery Partnerships Framework 2 ("
DPF2
") following the completion of the standstill period and signing of the DPF2 framework agreement.
DPF2 is a four-year framework intended to support the development and delivery of future technology solutions across the full lifecycle of Met Office products & services. Made Tech was successful in all three lots for which it tendered, providing the Group with potential future contract wins as contracts are awarded over the four year term, broken down as follows:
●
Lot 1 - Data
- £9 million, one of three suppliers supporting the Met Office's strategic data platforms and wider ecosystem.
●
Lot 3 - Secure Services
- £12 million, one of three suppliers supporting requirements within higher-security environments, including defence-related activities.
●
Lot 4 - Applications
- £47 million, one of five suppliers covering the development, support and lifecycle management of a wide range of applications supporting Met Office products and services.
At this stage no contracts have been awarded to Made Tech under DPF2 and contract wins will be announced as appropriate. As is customary with public sector frameworks of this nature, there is no guaranteed level of expenditure or revenue attributable to Made Tech, with individual programmes of work to be awarded under the framework over its four-year term.
The Group considers its selection as one of the suppliers to 'Lot 3 - Secure Services' to be of particular strategic importance. The lot covers work requiring higher levels of security clearance, including requirements relating to Defence. Made Tech's appointment therefore provides a route to compete for a broader range of higher-security government work and represents important progress in the Group's strategy to build its presence in the Defence sector, leveraging the capabilities and experience it has developed across Public Safety and Central Government.
Rory MacDonald, CEO of Made Tech, commented
:
"We are delighted to have been selected as a supplier to all three lots targeted under the Met Office's new Delivery Partnerships Framework 2.
We believe we are well placed to capitalise on the framework as a long-standing strategic partner of the Met Office, following successful deliveries, in particular the recent National Weather App where Made Tech and the Met Office jointly won the National Technology Awards: Public Sector Project of Year Award 2026
.
Expanding and deepening our existing client relationships is a key growth driver, alongside new client wins, and this selection underscores the progress we are making across both fronts."

latest.title: Made Tech secures largest contract in its history
latest.content:
18 Aug 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 0300R
Made Tech Group PLC
18 August 2026
MADE TECH GROUP PLC
("Made Tech" or the "Group")
Made Tech secures largest contract in its history
Upgrading Revenue and EBITDA guidance for the second time in 2026
London, 18 August 2026
-
Made Tech Group Plc
, (AIM:MTEC) a leading provider of digital, data and technology services to the UK public sector, is pleased to announce that it has been appointed as part of a consortium to a significant new four-year contract with a UK government department. The total contract value attributable to Made Tech is expected to be approximately £40 million over the life of the four-year contract award (the "
Award
"), making it the largest contract award in the Company's history.
Revenue from the Award is expected to commence in FY27, with a more significant contribution expected in FY28. As a result, the Board now expects revenue for FY27 to be in the range of £63 million to £66 million and adjusted EBITDA for FY27 to be in the range of £6.3 million to £6.6 million, ahead of current market expectations.* The Group will be reporting its FY26 final results in September and will provide further colour on the outlook at this stage.
As announced in its recent trading update, sales bookings accelerated significantly in H226. Together with the Award, this has increased the current Contracted Backlog to approximately £115 million, providing increased revenue visibility into FY27 and beyond
.
Rory MacDonald, CEO of Made Tech, commented:
"This is the largest contract award in our history and marks an important milestone in our growth.
The award also endorses our position at the centre of a number of critical programmes across government. Importantly, it also provides greater visibility over future revenues and underpins the Board's confidence in upgrading its expectations for FY27 while reinforcing our confidence in the Group's medium-term growth trajectory. We look forward to working alongside our consortium partners over the coming years."
*
Current market expectations prior to this announcement for FY27 were revenue of £60.3 million and adjusted EBITDA of £6.0 million.

Rory MacDonald, Chief Executive Officer, commented:
"FY26 has been a transformational year for Made Tech. We have delivered strong revenue growth, materially improved profitability and cash generation, and have entered FY27 with significant positive momentum in our business. The UK public sector is entering a multi-decade AI transformation, creating a substantial long-term opportunity for trusted delivery partners like Made Tech. Recent contract awards reinforce our position at the centre of a number of critical programmes across government. With a strong balance sheet, high earnings visibility and an increasingly differentiated proposition, we believe Made Tech is well positioned to capitalise on these opportunities and we look forward to FY27 with confidence."

company_30s.what_they_do: MTEC (Made Tech) designs and supplies advanced weather‑prediction software and hardware to government and commercial customers, helping them forecast climate events and manage risk.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The UK government’s push for better climate resilience and the growing demand for accurate weather data put MTEC in a niche with strong, long‑term contracts. Its systems are embedded in national weather services and critical infrastructure projects, giving it a defensible moat.
company_30s.current_state: MTEC has just landed its biggest contract ever and secured a multi‑year framework with the Met Office. It is in a growth phase, expanding its product line and customer base, while the stock has been hit by a sharp sell‑off that wiped out most of its market value.

rns_narrative: The company’s latest filings show a dramatic shift from a modest service provider to a key partner for national weather forecasting. The Met Office framework and the £68m contract over four years signal a new revenue stream and a long‑term partnership.

Earlier this year, MTEC announced it would release FY26 results ahead of the market’s expectations, hinting at stronger earnings. The company’s leadership changes, including a new CFO, suggest a strategic realignment to support the upcoming contracts.
These moves together paint a picture of a company that is pivoting from a small, cash‑burning start‑up to a contract‑heavy, revenue‑generating entity with a clear path to profitability.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism: traders are silent but watching for the next big win.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls point to the Met Office deal and the FY26 results as catalysts that could lift the stock to new highs. They see the contract as a sign that the company’s technology is now a core part of government infrastructure.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the company’s current valuation is too low and that the market will still be skeptical about whether the new contracts can generate the expected cash flow. They fear a continued sell‑off if earnings miss expectations.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Sentiment is shifting from complete indifference to cautious excitement. The community has been quiet, but the recent announcements are starting to spark conversation and a small wave of bullish chatter.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends shows no recent search interest, which is a perfect recipe for a surprise rebound when the catalysts materialise.

near_term_catalysts: Release of FY26 results in September – a positive earnings surprise could trigger a price rally.
Official announcement of the Met Office framework – confirming the start of the four‑year contract will give the stock a clear directional push.
Any sign of increased volume at key support levels (e.g., the 200‑day moving average) will indicate that traders are taking positions and that the crash is likely over.
expect_next.watch_for: Monitor the earnings release for guidance on cash flow and the timeline of the new contracts. Watch for a sudden spike in trading volume and a break above the recent low – that would confirm a mean‑reversion move.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock is still in the early stage of the crash‑recovery cycle. The APEX score suggests a tight compression, meaning a breakout could happen with a relatively small price move. A break above the recent low would signal that capitulation is finished.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The signal is a GREEN deep‑crash bottom, historically delivering a 39% average return. If the stock rebounds to the middle of its 52‑week range, that is roughly a 100% upside relative to its current level. The contract wins and earnings beat give a clear catalyst for a reversal, and the market’s silence maximises the surprise factor.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The downside is that the company still needs to prove it can deliver the new contracts on time and that the FY26 results will exceed expectations. If earnings fall short, the price could stay flat or decline further, leaving the trade in the red.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is limited to the current price (virtually zero). Upside could be 2‑3 times that if the stock reaches the mid‑range. The asymmetry is clearly favourable for a long position.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the price clears the recent low and volume spikes above the 20‑day average. Size the position to risk only 0.5% of capital per trade and place a stop 5% below the entry. Target the mid‑range of the 52‑week band, adjusting for any new support discovered.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for the FY26 results or the official Met Office framework announcement. A clear positive surprise or confirmation of the contract’s start date would be the trigger.
playbook.if_passing: None identified – there is no imminent delisting, bankruptcy or fraud risk.

ai_insights.bottom_line: MTEC is a deep‑crashed stock that has just secured a massive government contract; if the earnings beat and the contract launch come through, the upside is huge while the downside is virtually nil.
